on-sest-tous-defile.desc: A rare short done in much of the same vein of “Puissance de la Parole”, where there is no shortage of cross-dissolve and rapid montage effects. Here, the sources are between fashion clips, street footage, and a number of paintings, to which Godard narrates the implications of what is being seen.

on-solid-ground.title: On Solid Ground
on-solid-ground.desc: Summertime in a city. The coolness of a morning swim in the river quickly vanishes as the heat exacerbates insignificant daily nuisances. As Eli tires to escape the narrowness and agitation of the city, she keeps on facing aggression. Her rage starts to build up.

on-the-barricade.title: On the Barricade
on-the-barricade.desc: During the Paris Commune, a boy runs across trouble at the barricade. The film is now attributed to Alice Guy-Blaché by the Gaumont company, although there is some debate about whether it was directed by Étienne Arnaud.

on-the-border-2018.title: On the Border
on-the-border-2018.desc: A Korean teen named Hua Dongxing decides to leave his remote village. To realize his desire, he goes in town looking for his father and asking for travel expenses. This search takes him on a wondering roam.

on-the-edge-1998.title: On the Edge
on-the-edge-1998.desc: The film subjects the cross-section of the life of a family living on the edge of a city and the curiousity of their little son about it.

on-the-edge-1951.title: On the Edge
on-the-edge-1951.desc: In this fragile yet frightening poetic fantasy set against a dark industrial landscape, a woman sits knitting on the porch of her home when a man appears and takes the knitting from her.

on-the-edge-of-lisbon.title: On the Edge of Lisbon
on-the-edge-of-lisbon.desc: During the low tides, the Tagus estuary is an extraordinary place. The boats are resting on the sand. The vase of the river is revealed, black and thick. Vasco da Gama's bridge seems to move towards the continent. On the horizon, we guess some silhouettes. Sometimes those are flamingos. At other times, those are clams gleaners coming to work by hundreds.

on-the-everyday-use-of-the-eyes-of-death.title: On the Everyday Use of the Eyes of Death
on-the-everyday-use-of-the-eyes-of-death.desc: Filmed in Italy (Rome), on Agfa-Gaevert reversal film. Beavers destroyed the camera original.

on-the-pond.title: On the Pond
on-the-pond.desc: “Hoffman’s film is in the experimental film tradition of the personal diary although in this case a beautifully paced mixture of family photographs and dramatic reconstruction interwoven into a narrative that creates objective distance." (Michael O’Pray)

sur-les-rails.title: Sur les rails
sur-les-rails.desc: Maddened by jealousy, Jacques tries to kill his fellow worker.

on-the-roof.title: On the Roof
on-the-roof.desc: A group of Spanish boys take advantage of a high roof to ogle a sunbathing woman, but the presence of an adjacent male nude complicates matters.

on-the-roof-1897.title: On the Roof
on-the-roof-1897.desc: Two crooks throw a lady off a roof, and a hapless policeman tries to capture them.

on-the-set-the-life-aquatic-with-steve-z.title: On the Set: 'The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou'
on-the-set-the-life-aquatic-with-steve-z.desc: Director Wes Anderson and The Life Aquatic crew discuss the effort that went into crafting the world of Steve Zissou. Join us as we dive deep into the costumes, set design, and visual effects of this wild action adventure film.

on-the-trail-of-the-iguana.title: On the Trail of the Iguana
on-the-trail-of-the-iguana.desc: Behind the scenes documentary of the filming of Tennessee Williams' The Night of the Iguana.

on-xerxes-throne.title: On Xerxes' Throne
on-xerxes-throne.desc: A dystopian workplace at the Perama shipyard. A ban on physical contact has turned human interaction into otherworldly simulations. The suppression of touch has alienated the workers communication transforming the boatyard into a charged landscape of alienation and repressed sensuality beyond stereotypical heteronormative desires. According to local legend, the Persian King Xerxes watched the overwhelming defeat of his fleet from his throne on the rocky peaks of Mount Egaleo, in today’s Perama.

on-line-1976.title: On-Line
on-line-1976.desc: Musicians and dancer perform in real-time while Schwartz plays a computer-keyboard to create special effects on a computer-controlled video-visual communication system.

onan.title: Onan
onan.desc: “ONAN is a work about desire (masturbation) which has no object but itself. The appearance of the large egg objectifies the man's desires. After colliding with the other (a girl), the hero falls down while still holding the egg, thus caricaturing the desire of the hero.” —Takahiko Iimura (takaiimura.com)

once-and-forever.title: Once and Forever
once-and-forever.desc: A biographical short about French fashion designer Gabrielle "Coco" Chanel.

once-i-kept-quiet-for-a-whole-session.title: Once I Kept Quiet For a Whole Session
once-i-kept-quiet-for-a-whole-session.desc: Tuna is taking a course to become a writer. Under the influence of her mother, thinking it will benefit her, she starts psychotherapy. As she starts to tell about herself and what she is going through, she starts avoiding them. Her relationship with her roommate is also affected in the process.

once-upon-a-line.title: Once Upon a Line
once-upon-a-line.desc: A man leads a monotone, humdrum existence until he meets somebody.

once-upon-a-snowman.title: Once Upon a Snowman
once-upon-a-snowman.desc: The previously untold origins of Olaf, the innocent and insightful, summer-loving snowman are revealed as we follow Olaf’s first steps as he comes to life and searches for his identity in the snowy mountains outside Arendelle.

once-upon-a-time-1957.title: Once Upon a Time
once-upon-a-time-1957.desc: An oddball pair try to find their identity and place in an abstract world.

once-upon-a-time-1973-1.title: Once Upon a Time
once-upon-a-time-1973-1.desc: We are first presented a cobweb castle, filled with the haunting doubts of the young protagonist. Spirits appear on the screen and are heard on the soundtrack. Gradually a female guide emerges and escorts the young man into an antechamber to another (and possibly higher) world.

once-upon-a-time-there-lived-a-dog.title: Once Upon a Time, There Lived a Dog
once-upon-a-time-there-lived-a-dog.desc: Based on the Ukrainian folktale, the old dog of a village family is not as keen as he once was, and is sent away after he fails to guard their house during a robbery. In the woods, he meets the wolf he protected his masters against long ago, who decides to pay a favor to get his old enemy's rightful place back in the doghouse.

once-upon-a-wintertime.title: Once Upon a Wintertime
once-upon-a-wintertime.desc: A short segment of the feature film Melody Time, re-released as a separate entity five years afterwards.

one-1966.title: One
one-1966.desc: Collected as part of the Fluxfilm Anthology (a multi-reel compendium of 37 short films assembled by Fluxus founder and central operator George Maciunas), One captures the lifespan of a single match recorded at 2,000 frames per second using a 16mm high-speed camera. The frame rate is then decelerated to the standard 24fps for presentation. The film emphasizes each gesture, sway and flare of flame as the small pinewood carrier ignites across the landscape of the filmstrip and screen, signalling the drama and poetics of this ”minor” event before the fire is extinguished. One also stands as an unassuming beacon, immortalizing on film the essence of some of Ono’s early concerns as an artist. At…

one-breath-around-the-world.title: One Breath Around The World
one-breath-around-the-world.desc: Free diver Guillaume Néry swims to the depths of the oceans, and allows us to explore a world that is usually out of reach.

one-by-one.title: One by One
one-by-one.desc: In a place in Africa we follow a group of children preparing their kites for an adventure of their life. The short was intended to be one of the segments for the proposed but never completed Fantasia 2006.

one-cabs-family.title: One Cab's Family
one-cabs-family.desc: A happily married pair of taxicabs are delighted when Junior enters their lives, but this delight turns to consternation when he states his ambition to become a hotrodder..

one-day-2012.title: One Day
one-day-2012.desc: One man always on the move will have an encounter that puts into question everything he knows.
one-day-2012.director: Joël Corcia, Bernard Som, Thomas Reteuna, Laurent Rossi, Bung Nguyen

one-day-a-man-bought-a-house.title: One Day a Man Bought a House
one-day-a-man-bought-a-house.desc: A man buys a house on a hill. A rat was there first, and proves to be unusually difficult to remove; it seems to think all the man's attempts to kill it are actually gifts. It loves the taste of the poison, thinks the trap is a sculpture, and so forth.

one-day-2001.title: One Day...
one-day-2001.desc: After he gets out of the toilets, a man is being chased by a human-sized turd, claiming to be the man's child. "Why have you abandoned me?" is the question the turd keeps on asking. First, the man is embarrassed by the annoying presence of the turd, then he slowly accepts it alongside him...

one-droopy-knight.title: One Droopy Knight
one-droopy-knight.desc: Sir Droopalot and Sir Butchalot (Droopy and Butch) vie with each other to kill a dragon that is terrorizing their kingdom. Whomever vanquishes the dragon will marry the king's daughter.

one-flight-up.title: One Flight Up
one-flight-up.desc: ONE FLIGHT UP is both the name of this documentary portrait and the title of a piece by artist Alex Katz. The work-of-the-same-name figures prominently (or, more accurately, entirely) in the film-of-the-same-name.

one-frame-duration.title: One Frame Duration
one-frame-duration.desc: The films concerns the "duration" (or non-duration) of one frame, as the title indicates, the minimum unit of film in space (dark and light) with sound (or silent) and their various combinations.

one-froggy-evening.title: One Froggy Evening
one-froggy-evening.desc: A workman finds a singing frog in the cornerstone of an old building being demolished. But when he tries to cash in on his discovery, he finds the frog will sing only for him, and just croak for the talent agent and the audience in the theater he's spent his life savings on.

one-hams-family.title: One Ham's Family
one-hams-family.desc: A hungry wolf with ham in the shape of a pig kid stands in for Santa Claus.

one-hundred-a-day.title: One Hundred a Day
one-hundred-a-day.desc: A young girl is forced to continue working at her machine all day in a 1930s shoe factory after a visit to a backyard abortionist. Based on the short story 'How beautiful are thy feet' by Alan Marshall.

one-hundredth-of-a-second.title: One Hundredth of a Second
one-hundredth-of-a-second.desc: Kate is a talented photojournalist. She risks her life to deliver powerful images to the waiting world until a photograph of a Girl changes her life forever.

one-is-business-the-other-crime.title: One Is Business, the Other Crime
one-is-business-the-other-crime.desc: Griffith intercuts between the lives of two couples married on the same day. One couple is rich, the other poor. Time passes, and in desperation over joblessness, the poor husband attempts to burgle a home, only to be captured at gunpoint by the mistress of the house. It is the home of the rich couple. While holding the poor intruder at gunpoint, the rich wife accidentally discovers evidence implicating her own husband in a bribery scheme.

one-man-band.title: One Man Band
one-man-band.desc: With one coin to make a wish at the piazza fountain, a peasant girl encounters two competing street performers who'd prefer the coin find its way into their tip jars. The little girl, Tippy, is caught in the middle as a musical duel ensues between the one-man-bands.

one-minute-puberty.title: One Minute Puberty
one-minute-puberty.desc: A great way to describe in a minute what it's like to be a boy going through puberty.

one-minute-time-machine.title: One-Minute Time Machine
one-minute-time-machine.desc: Every time the beautiful Regina rejects his advances, James pushes a red button and tries again, all the while unaware of the reality and consequences of his actions.

one-more-time-1931.title: One More Time
one-more-time-1931.desc: Foxy the Cop is trying to enforce the law in town, but dangerous drivers and strangers who also kidnap Roxy are making this difficult.

one-of-many-places-in-which-something-wa.title: One of Many Places in Which Something Was Stolen
one-of-many-places-in-which-something-wa.desc: Shot in 16mm on a turret Bolex, One of Many Places in Which Something Was Stolen is an experimental short film that takes place along an ice-covered pond, concentrating on an incident involving a masked assailant and a young woman.
one-of-many-places-in-which-something-wa.director: Eli Hayes, Amy Jacobson, Jesse Rolfe

one-of-those-days-1988.title: One of Those Days
one-of-those-days-1988.desc: A day in the life of the world's unluckiest guy. Starting the morning off with a shaving nick from hell, he endures fires, mad dogs, rampaging vacuum cleaners, horny neighbors, kids with ray guns and, of course, a steam-roller.

one-one.title: One One
one-one.desc: The philosopher is a child born under the divorce of being and thinking.

one-piece-dream-soccer-king.title: One Piece: Dream Soccer King!
one-piece-dream-soccer-king.desc: At a huge pillar stadium, the Grand Line Cup Final is being held. The "Straw Hat Pirate Team"(Luffy, Zoro, Usopp, Sanji, and Chopper) are having a tie breaker shoot out against the "Villian All Star Team"(Buggy, Bon Clay, Jango, Hatchan, and a soccer like head player named Odacchi). Everyone of them gets a turn in kicking the ball to the goal. While Coby is taking the goalie position, and isn't doing too good in blocking the goal. One after another, the game eventually comes to a sudden death match. Which team will win the Grand Line Cup?

one-piece-jangos-dance-carnival.title: One Piece: Jango's Dance Carnival
one-piece-jangos-dance-carnival.desc: The Straw Hat Pirates visit Mirrorball Island. Where a big dance carnival is being held. Jango the Hypnotist was there too, to show off his dance moves. Only when he was found by a group of Marines who were about to arrest him. But ended up chasing him throughout the island. Our heroes got involved when one of the Marines recognized Luffy from the wanted poster. And they end up getting chased as well. Soon Jango steals the spotlight of the dance carnival and uses his hypnosis on everyone on the island. And soon everyone including Jango, The StrawHat Pirates, and the marines are all dancing like there's no tomorrow.

one-please.title: One Please
one-please.desc: Parents will do anything for their children.

one-rat-short.title: One Rat Short
one-rat-short.desc: A city rat pursues a nearly empty bag of cheese snacks that's drifting in the breeze. His journey takes him through a vent into a highly mechanized rat lab, where one particular white female gets his attention.

one-red-nose-day-and-a-wedding.title: One Red Nose Day and a Wedding
one-red-nose-day-and-a-wedding.desc: You’re invited to the wedding of the year, as the original cast of Four Weddings and a Funeral reunite in this one-off sequel. Twenty-five years after the events of Four Weddings and a Funeral (1994), Charles, Carrie, Fiona, Tom, David, Matthew, Bernard, Lydia and Father Gerald are back in church. But whose wedding is it - and will there be any more familiar faces?

the-one-romantic-venture-of-edward.title: The One Romantic Venture of Edward
the-one-romantic-venture-of-edward.desc: The young man, played by Stan Brakhage, gets himself into a seriously comic mix-up by indulging in semi-sexual fantasies, and allowing the fantasies to take over. This is the best of my very early films and includes my first footage.

one-small-step-2018.title: One Small Step
one-small-step-2018.desc: ​Luna is a vibrant young Chinese-American girl who dreams of becoming an astronaut. From the day she witnesses a rocket launching into space on TV, Luna is driven to reach for the stars. In the big city, Luna lives with her loving father Chu, who supports her with a humble shoe repair business he runs out of his garage. As Luna grows up, she enters college, facing adversity of all kinds in pursuit of her dreams.

one-way-to-find-out.title: One Way to Find Out
one-way-to-find-out.desc: Hand-printed sections from 35mm movie trailers create a chaotic and densely layered retelling of Hollywood form. Loosely about desire, fear of coupling, and the consequences of moving forward, with results both catastrophic and ecstatic.

one-wheel-dance.title: One Wheel Dance
one-wheel-dance.desc: Condit's son Lloyd Vogel unicycling on a beautiful fall day.

one-eyed-men-are-kings.title: One-Eyed Men Are Kings
one-eyed-men-are-kings.desc: One-Eyed Men Are Kings [Les... borgnes sont rois] is a 1974 French short film directed by Michel Leroy and Edmond Séchan. In the film, a sad middle-aged man in Paris man and his dog go for a walk, which turns into an ordeal. The film won an Oscar for Best Live Action Short Film.

the-one-man-band.title: The One-Man Band
the-one-man-band.desc: A band-leader has arranged seven chairs for the members of his band. When he sits down in the first chair, a cymbal player appears in the same chair, then rises and sits in the next chair. As the cymbal player sits down, a drummer appears in the second chair, and then likewise moves on to the third chair. In this way, an entire band is soon formed, and is then ready to perform.

onesime-clockmaker.title: Onesime, Clockmaker
onesime-clockmaker.desc: In an effort to secure a promised inheritance, Onésime invents a time machine that speeds up activity on earth, hyper-animates men and machines, and telescopes the human life-cycle.

only-blood-relates-us.title: Only Blood Relates Us
only-blood-relates-us.desc: Four storylines where characters prepare for an undisclosed event on the same day in which there seem to be secretive and seemingly sinister intentions. Faced with mysterious memories and strange circumstances, the narrative slowly reveals the way in which the characters are connected and what their visions have summed up to.

only-me.title: Only Me
only-me.desc: A well-dressed but inebriated man decides to attend a variety show at the Palace Theatre. During the show, both he and the performers are continually harassed by a practical joke-loving boy who is sitting in a box seat near the stage. Soon the inebriated man himself begins to cause disruptions, with his overly emphatic opinions of the various acts.

onesime-vs-onesime.title: Onésime vs. Onésime
onesime-vs-onesime.desc: His double behaves very badly, while the real Onésime suffers the consequences.

open-book.title: Open Book
open-book.desc: Acconci's open mouth is framed by the camera in an extreme close-up, bringing the viewer uncomfortably close. A desperate sense of strained urgency comes across as Acconci gasps, "I'll accept you, I won't shut down, I won't shut you out.... I'm open to you, I'm open to everything.... This is not a trap, we can go inside, yes, come inside...." Acconci continues to plead in this way for the length of the tape, his mouth held unnaturally wide open. The pathological psychology of such enforced openness betrays a desperate struggle to accept and be accepted by others. The sustained image of Acconci's open mouth also evidences a sinister, vaguely threatening streak that is more or less evident in…

open-score.title: Open Score
open-score.desc: 1966 experimental short work by Robert Rauschenberg

open-the-door.title: Open the Door
open-the-door.desc: Practically a home movie, Lena (Dunham) asks her parents to say specific lines for a film she's shooting while they request to be let in her apartment.

the-open-window.title: The Open Window
the-open-window.desc: In the middle of his crazy day, a man tries to remember if he closed a window at home.

opening-day-of-close-up.title: Opening Day of Close-Up
opening-day-of-close-up.desc: At his cinema in Rome, the Nuovo Sacher, Nanni Moretti anxiously oversees preparations for the premiere of the film Close-up, by Iranian director Abbas Kiarostami. Meanwhile Disney's The Lion King is taking Italy by storm.

opening-speech.title: Opening Speech
opening-speech.desc: Norman McLaren attempts to give the opening speech for the first Montreal International Film Festival, but his microphone won't cooperate.

opera-2020.title: Opera
opera-2020.desc: The history, structures and rhythms of human history are seen through a glorious, massive pyramid.

opera-no-1.title: Opera No. 1
opera-no-1.desc: A comical mini opera following the exploits of two goddesses interfering with the lives of mortals. Mistaken identities, miscast spells, and rollerblades abound.

operation-x-70.title: Operation X-70
operation-x-70.desc: A powerful nation has experimented with a new gas, which does not kill or injure the asphyxiated subjects, only puts them in a lethargic and mystical state. X-70 gas bombs will be dropped by mistake over Nebelux and provoke an unexpected mutation of the population of this friendly little country. (miff.com.au)

operation-rabbit.title: Operation: Rabbit
operation-rabbit.desc: Wile E. Coyote, genius, announces to Bugs Bunny that he is going to catch him and eat him, and then employs a variety of gadgets and plans in an attempt to do so.

operator-2015.title: Operator
operator-2015.desc: An Emergency Services Operator in a Fire Control Room has just started a long night shift when she picks up a call from a desperate young mother. An hour previously, Gemma had fallen asleep in front of the television and has now woken to find the room full of smoke. Her three year old son is trapped in his bedroom upstairs. Flames have started to creep down the stairs that Gemma must use in order to reach him. The operator’s guidance is all that Gemma can rely on in order to survive.

ophelia-1969.title: Ophelia
ophelia-1969.desc: A portrait inspired by reading about John Millais' painting Ophelia.

opium-den.title: Opium Den
opium-den.desc: A century-old film depicting opium smokers in French Indochina (Vietnam).

oppressed-majority.title: Oppressed Majority
oppressed-majority.desc: On what seems to be just another ordinary day, a man is exposed to sexism and sexual violence in a society ruled by women.

the-opry-house.title: The Opry House
the-opry-house.desc: Mickey runs a small theatre. The orchestra plays, rather badly, excerpts from Carmen. Mickey appears as a snake charmer, but the snake is revealed to be a cat with a snake's head painted on its tail. Mickey does a belly dance, to the audience's delight. Mickey then plays the piano, but the piano and stool, apparently annoyed at the violence and complexity of the piece, kick him off stage.

the-opry-house-1929.title: The Opry House
the-opry-house-1929.desc: The Mound City Blue Blowers and Doris Walker perform popular songs of the day.

an-optical-poem.title: An Optical Poem
an-optical-poem.desc: A dance of shapes. A title card tells us this is an experiment in conveying the mental images of music in a visual form. Liszt's "Second Hungarian Rhapsody" is the music. The shapes, all two-dimensional, are circles primarily, with some squares and rectangles, and a few triangles. The shapes move rhythmically to the music: receding from view or moving across the screen. Red circles on a blue background; light blue squares; white rectangles. Then, a red background of many circles with a few in the foreground. Red gives way to blue then to white. Shapes reappear as Liszt's themes re-occur. Then, with a few staccato notes and images, it's over.

optimism.title: Optimism
optimism.desc: The urge to relieve a winter valley of permanent shadow and find gold in alluvial gravel is part of a long history of desire and extraction in the far Canadian north. Cancan dancers, curlers, smelters, former city officials, and a curious cliff-side mirrored disc congregate to form a town portrait. Shot on location in Dawson City, Yukon Territory.

opus-5.title: Opus #5
opus-5.desc: A sinister montage intimates the hellish void facing a man emptying bottles by the river. Sandy Fisher’s densely reverberating electronic score provides strong support for Lloyd Williams’ cultic collage of skulls, chess boards and fire.

opus-40.title: Opus 40
opus-40.desc: Opus 40” is about repetition: repetition in working and living, repetition through multiplicity and series, repetition to form pattern and rhythm, repetition in order and in revealing.

opus-74-version-2.title: Opus 74, Version 2
opus-74-version-2.desc: Single frame exposures, color. Different image each frame, various items in the room, etc.

lightplay-opus-ii.title: Lightplay Opus II
lightplay-opus-ii.desc: An abstract animation from Walter Ruttmann.

opus-iii.title: Opus III
opus-iii.desc: An abstract animation from Walter Ruttmann.

opus-iv.title: Opus IV
opus-iv.desc: An abstract animation by Walter Ruttmann.

ora.title: ORA
ora.desc: Dancer in three dimensions and glowing from the inside.

the-oracle-of-delphi.title: The Oracle of Delphi
the-oracle-of-delphi.desc: A box of valued jewels is placed inside the tomb of Delphi. A thief breaks into the tomb and steals it, but soon the ghost of Delphi appears and puts a curse on him.

oramunde.title: Oramunde
oramunde.desc: Early dance film filmed outdoors and directed by artist Emlen Etting.

orange-2003.title: Orange
orange-2003.desc: ORANGE is inspired by the direct film (cameraless) tradition. This tradition includes works in which the filmstrip is directly manipulated by painting, scratching, or otherwise placing objects on it. This tradition was probably originated by Len Lye in his hand painted A COLOUR BOX from 1935. To create his piece, Gregg Biermann cut up an orange into several pieces and scanned the pieces into his computer. He then took the image files of the orange pieces and “pasted” them directly into the video strip using a photo editing software package. This technique then transforms the orange pieces into what appears to be a random exploding jumble of images when viewed.

orange-1970.title: Orange
orange-1970.desc: A study of a girl eating an orange.

the-orange-hid-its-purple.title: the orange hid its purple
the-orange-hid-its-purple.desc: A three minute contemplative/ambient piece that's primarily a study of contrasts & fusions between the colors orange and purple (hence the title), incorporating elements of water, naturalism and (sub)urbanism.

oranges.title: Oranges
oranges.desc: Two boys are talking after a bicycle accident. The older is bragging about his experience with girls, but is that just a boast?

orb.title: Orb
orb.desc: A compact, full-color cut-out animation as ephemeral as the colors swimming on the surface of a soap bubble. The eternal round shape, the orb (sun, moon, symbol of the whole self) balloons its inimitable and joyous course through scene after scene of celestial delight, fixing at last as the mystical globe encasing the lovers whose course it has paralleled throughout the film.

the-orchestra-2016.title: The Orchestra
the-orchestra-2016.desc: In a world filled with beautiful and harmonious music, elderly Vernon always seems to strike the wrong note.

the-order-of-ideas-at-the-leslie-street-.title: The Order of Ideas at the Leslie Street Spit
the-order-of-ideas-at-the-leslie-street-.desc: On the paths that cut through Toronto's Tommy Thompson Park, at the foot of Leslie Street, an assortment of terrains collide: thicket, pebbled shorelines, muddy vistas, and fertile earth with beds of wildflowers. A giant duck crosses the horizon. A radio transmission of Shooby Taylor, the human horn, travels with us.

orgosolos-shepherds.title: Orgosolo’s Shepherds
orgosolos-shepherds.desc: The striking landscapes of rural Sardinia provide the backdrop to this lyrical look at the hardscrabble lives of the region’s shepherds in winter.

the-origin-of-captain-america.title: The Origin of Captain America
the-origin-of-captain-america.desc: A young man reads a comic depicting what the title says. We see his face and reactions. He finally finishes the book and leaves the scene.

the-origin-of-stitch.title: The Origin of Stitch
the-origin-of-stitch.desc: Stitch discovers Jumba’s secret computer that reveals what creatures Jumba had used to create Stitch, and also hints at his other 625 experiments. Stitch is scared to find out what a monster he is, only for Jumba to come and explain how he found love when he met Lilo.

the-original-movie.title: The Original Movie
the-original-movie.desc: A prehistoric writer sells his masterpiece to a film company, which is butchered horribly in the process of getting made into a stone-age movie. Preserved by the Academy Film Archive in 2010.

the-originals-2022.title: The Originals
the-originals-2022.desc: Matty "Square" Ruggiero and his childhood friends tell their story of what it was like to grow up in South Brooklyn, where money was tight but friendships were tighter.

tomorrowland-the-origins-of-plus-ultra.title: Tomorrowland: The Origins of Plus Ultra
tomorrowland-the-origins-of-plus-ultra.desc: A diegetic history of the secret Plus Ultra society from Disney's Tomorrowland movie. Animated by Pixar artists, narrated by Maurice LeMarche as Orson Welles, directed by Brad Bird, and written by Brad Bird, Damon Lindelof, and Jeff Jensen. Originally previewed in an unfinished form at the Walt Disney Pictures panel at D23 Expo 2019, first released in two halves on the Take Me To Tomorrowland promotional website. Originally intended to be placed within the film as a multimedia dark-ride attraction when young Frank Walker plunges beneath "it's a small world", it was cut and then appended as a pre-film short in a limited number of cinemas during its theatrical release. The option to play this…

orphans-benefit-1934.title: Orphan's Benefit
orphans-benefit-1934.desc: Donald and Mickey put on a charity show, for some orphans.

orphans-picnic.title: Orphan's Picnic
orphans-picnic.desc: Mickey and Donald take a truckload of mouse boys on a picnic. The boys delight in tormenting Donald, first by filching the picnic food, then giving him a flower with a bee inside (Donald eventually gets the whole hive after him), and finally a sandwich with another bee in it.

the-orphan-2018.title: The Orphan
the-orphan-2018.desc: The story of Jonathas, an orphan who had been adopted and then "returned" due to his effeminate mannerisms.

orphans-benefit.title: Orphans' Benefit
orphans-benefit.desc: Mickey and friends put on a revue for the orphans. Donald recites nursery rhymes, but the orphans torment him. Horace, Goofy, and Clarabelle do a dance number. Donald tries again. Clara clucks a song while Mickey plays piano (with support from an unseen orchestra). Donald returns, and the orphans finally send a parade of bricks and eggs on balloons over him and use slingshots to drop them on his head.

orpheus-outtakes.title: Orpheus (Outtakes)
orpheus-outtakes.desc: “Using footage from Cocteau’s Orphée, Clark optically prints an interstitial space where the ghosts of cinema lurk beyond and within the frames.” – Andrea Picard

the-outlaws-1993.title: The Outlaws
the-outlaws-1993.desc: In the 40's, after the Spanish Civil War, many republicans defeated by the nationalist forces of Franco found refuge on the bordering mountains in the north of Portugal. Some saw them as brigands, others gave them shelter and helped them on the sly to police forces of Salazar. They were... the Outlaws.

oscar-wildes-the-nightingale-and-the-ros.title: Oscar Wilde's the Nightingale and the Rose
oscar-wildes-the-nightingale-and-the-ros.desc: A nightingale bird discovers a true lover when she witnesses a young university student talk with great passion about his beloved. The Nightingale goes on a quest to find the red rose the Student needs win his lovers heart, but this comes at a chilling price. Based on the classic fairytale by Oscar Wilde.

oscars-bell.title: Oscar's Bell
oscars-bell.desc: Duncan and four legged friend Oscar go camping as they often have, but this time something in the woods looks back at them.

oscars-hotel-for-fantastical-creatures.title: Oscar's Hotel for Fantastical Creatures
oscars-hotel-for-fantastical-creatures.desc: When the owner of Oscar's Hotel leaves on important business, he entrusts the establishment and its gallery of monstrous residents to his nephew Oliver - resulting in more than a little bit of chaos.

oskar-langenfeld-12-mal.title: Oskar Langenfeld. 12 Mal
oskar-langenfeld-12-mal.desc: Twelve short scenes of the life of an elderly homeless person, Oskar Langenfeld, in Berlin.

oskar-schlemmer-and-dance.title: Oskar Schlemmer and Dance
oskar-schlemmer-and-dance.desc: Original film material from the Bauhaus dances of Oskar Schlemmer.

oss-oss-wee-oss.title: Oss Oss Wee Oss
oss-oss-wee-oss.desc: Padstow, a fishing village on the coast of Cornwall, celebrates May Day with an ancient custom: two osses (hobby-horses) dance through the town streets accompanied by drums and accordions. All Padstownians participate in the event, which has now become a tourist attraction drawing over tens of thousands of annual visitors. Folklorists Alan Lomax and Peter Kennedy and filmmaker George Pickow collected footage at the festival in 1951, producing a pioneering work in the use of sound, low-light photography, and conversational presentation of narrative. A favorite of Margaret Mead, who used it in her classes, the film circulated widely and continues to have influence today, especially in the…

the-ossuary.title: The Ossuary
the-ossuary.desc: A non-narrative voyage round Sedlec Ossuary, which has been constructed from over 50,000 human skeletons (victims of the Black Death).

ostrich-politic.title: Ostrich Politic
ostrich-politic.desc: Ostriches carry on their daily activities burying their heads, believing it’s an instinctive behavior. However, one day research by phylogeneticist Dr. Kays proves otherwise.

an-ostrich-told-me-the-world-is-fake-and.title: An Ostrich Told Me the World Is Fake and I Think I Believe It
an-ostrich-told-me-the-world-is-fake-and.desc: When a young telemarketer is confronted by a mysterious talking ostrich, he learns that the universe is stop motion animation. He must put aside his dwindling toaster sales and focus on convincing his colleagues of his terrifying discovery. It's scary business living in a stop motion world, where your faces come off and a giant hand controls your every move.

ostriches.title: Ostriches
ostriches.desc: An ostrich pulls a cart carrying young women wearing ostrich-feather hats.

oswald-the-lucky-rabbit.title: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit
oswald-the-lucky-rabbit.desc: For the first time in nearly 95 years, Oswald stars in an all-new hand-drawn short from Walt Disney Animation Studios in celebration of Disney 100 Years of Wonder!

othello-1909.title: Othello
othello-1909.desc: Gerolamo Lo Savio's version of William Shakespeare's Othello.

the-other-also.title: The Other Also
the-other-also.desc: A minimalist, atmospheric, meditation on the theme of "Love" or "Amour" that focuses on reconciliation and forgiveness.

other-side-of-the-box.title: Other Side of the Box
other-side-of-the-box.desc: A couple receives a mysterious package from an old friend.

the-other-side-of-the-witching-hour.title: The Other Side of the Witching Hour
the-other-side-of-the-witching-hour.desc: A spellbinding journey into the mind of an insomniac, who spends each night haunted by strange and wonderful illusions from another world.

the-other-side-1994.title: The Other Side
the-other-side-1994.desc: A simple life of simple creatures in a wonderful and awful world.

other-worlds.title: Other Worlds
other-worlds.desc: A man and a woman, talking over their relationship.

the-other-1989.title: The Other
the-other-1989.desc: Documentary about the joys and sorrows of being trans.

others-will-follow.title: Others Will Follow
others-will-follow.desc: The lone survivor of the first mission to the surface of Mars uses his last moments to transmit an important photo.

the-ouija-board.title: The Ouija Board
the-ouija-board.desc: Max Fleischer draws Koko and a haunted house, while his colleague and the janitor mess around with a Ouija board. When Max goes over to take a look, Koko is haunted by ghosts and inanimate objects, and escapes into the real-world studio.

oumoun.title: Oumoun
oumoun.desc: "Dear grandma, you’ll be surprised to hear my voice in your language…'" In Oumoun Brussels filmmaker Fairuz Ghammam plays the recording of a spoken letter that was never sent to her elderly grandmother in Mahdia, Tunisia. In the company of the camera, the lines become a voice over, as we witness a dialogue across languages, across cultures, across generations.

an-ounce-of-pink.title: An Ounce of Pink
an-ounce-of-pink.desc: The Pink Panther encounters a coin-operated talking weight and fortune machine which suggests that he bring it home with him on the basis of it being a valuable asset - it doesn't go so well.

our-baseball-game.title: Our Baseball Game
our-baseball-game.desc: A baseball game between the rabbits and tanuki (raccoon dogs).

our-day.title: Our Day
our-day.desc: Home movie of the day in the life of the Kelly Family of Lebanon, Kentucky.

our-former-glory.title: Our Former Glory
our-former-glory.desc: A fantasy taking its cue from reliquary objects left to rot along the Brooklyn Promenade, overlooking the site of the former World Trade Center Towers. The film proposes visual similes between impersonal architecture and the language of mass production that define America's most pervasive global export: a living aesthetic culture of utility. Just as we can conceive of sentimental or spiritual offerings as disposable, so too are we led to identify our selves within that aesthetic.

our-gay-brothers.title: Our Gay Brothers
our-gay-brothers.desc: This collage of found film footage, assembles porn movie, children's instructional film, sports coverage, and '50s Hollywood musicals to construct an investigation of gay men's differing attitudes towards the female body.

our-kind-of-love.title: Our Kind of Love
our-kind-of-love.desc: Samira, an Afghan village girl, is on her first date in London.

our-lady-of-the-sphere.title: Our Lady of the Sphere
our-lady-of-the-sphere.desc: Our Lady of the Sphere uses cut-out animation to craft a bizarre science fiction experiment. Moving spheres, such as balloons and bubbles, are superimposed on static backgrounds to suggest travel and discovery.

our-new-errand-boy.title: Our New Errand Boy
our-new-errand-boy.desc: A mischievous errand boy, sent out on a delivery, causes havoc in the streets of Hove. When he arrives back at the shop, he finds all his furious victims are already there complaining to the grocer -- and the chase is on!

our-summer-made-her-light-escape.title: Our Summer Made Her Light Escape
our-summer-made-her-light-escape.desc: A wordless portrait of interiority, maternal ambivalence and the passage of time.

our-ten-years.title: Our Ten Years
our-ten-years.desc: Throughout ten years of a key era in Chinese and Hong Kong history, a girl becomes fixated on a fellow commuter who she observes regularly. While the two never speak to one another, the girl captures her appearance and life changes during the years through various means such as photos and drawings.

our-time-is-up.title: Our Time Is Up
our-time-is-up.desc: When therapist Dr. Leonard Stern discovers he has six weeks to live, he adopts a fresh method of treatment: brutal honesty.

our-trip-to-africa.title: Our Trip to Africa
our-trip-to-africa.desc: Originally commissioned by an Austrian couple in 1961 to photograph a travel diary documenting their wild game hunt, Kubelka shot three hours of film and recorded fourteen hours of audio. Over the next few years, Kubelka toiled in the editing bay, producing a work charged with intricate, ironic brutality.

out-and-out-rout.title: Out and Out Rout
out-and-out-rout.desc: Wile E. Coyote chases the Road Runner using a skateboard, a hunting falcon, two doves tied to his feet.

out-of-a-forest.title: Out of a Forest
out-of-a-forest.desc: A family of rabbits are having a birthday party under a big tree, unaware that a mischievous wolf is approaching.

out-of-darkness-2013.title: Out of Darkness
out-of-darkness-2013.desc: A unique story told by nine different actors which explores the haunting of a conscience by lost souls that won't let go.

out-of-print-2008.title: Out of Print
out-of-print-2008.desc: An ode to the counterculture of the 80s and 90s, when finding quality culture was a real treasure hunt.

out-of-scale.title: Out of Scale
out-of-scale.desc: Donald has a ride-on sized train layout in his backyard. There's a large tree (home to Chip 'n Dale) that's out of scale, so Donald moves it while they're out; they come back to see their tree moving. No problem; one of Donald's model houses is just their size.

out-of-sight-2010.title: Out of Sight
out-of-sight-2010.desc: The main character of little girl in the story confronts a robbery and strays from the road she is familiar with. After passing a hedge, she enters an unknown world and unfolds a magical adventure depending on senses other than vision and her imagination. With soft and cute colors as the main key, we used simple designs to depict the little girls' imaginary world.

out-of-the-frying-pan-into-the-firing-li.title: Out of the Frying Pan Into the Firing Line
out-of-the-frying-pan-into-the-firing-li.desc: Documentary short film demonstrating the process by which waste fats from the kitchens of American homes can be transformed into the raw materials for explosives for the war effort.

out-of-the-inkwell.title: Out of the Inkwell
out-of-the-inkwell.desc: In a tribute to the Fleischer brothers shorts of the '20s, a janitor hypnotizes Max Fleischer's pen to draw Betty Boop.

out-of-the-inkwell-1919.title: Out of the Inkwell
out-of-the-inkwell-1919.desc: Max Fleischer draws the upper and lower halves of the Clown's body, which dance around separately before coming together. Max interacts with his creation before ultimately washing the Clown off the page with water.

out-of-the-law.title: Out of the Law
out-of-the-law.desc: Beyond all human restraint lies one's lugubrious layers of paint.

out-of-the-melting-pot.title: Out of the Melting Pot
out-of-the-melting-pot.desc: “Many early short subjects cloaked genuine aesthetic discourse inside novelty approaches, such as the exploration of slow, fast, or reverse motion, distortion and abstraction, and other altered perceptions induced via camera tricks. The transitions of zoo animals from abstract to realistic renditions highlight the differences between the two states.” - Bruce Posner

out-of-time-2012.title: Out of Time
out-of-time-2012.desc: Two time-traveling tourists from the future visit present day London.

out-on-a-limb.title: Out on a Limb
out-on-a-limb.desc: Donald's doing a little tree surgery when he spots Chip 'n' Dale gathering nuts. He saws off the branch outside their hole and paints it with tar, which Dale gets stuck in. Then Donald has a little fun with the long-handled pruning shears.

out-yonder-neighbor-boy.title: Out Yonder — Neighbor Boy
out-yonder-neighbor-boy.desc: Humorous short film in which David Lynch and his son Austin observe the follies of their neighbor.

out-yonder-teeth.title: Out Yonder — Teeth
out-yonder-teeth.desc: On a quiet winter morning, Austin, son of David Lynch, breaks his silence and decides to talk about his troubling functional incapacitation.

out-foxed.title: Out-Foxed
out-foxed.desc: Droopy is part of a pack of English hunting hounds trying unsuccessfully to catch a tricky, tea-drinking fox.

outerborough.title: Outerborough
outerborough.desc: In 1899, a photographer at American Mutoscope & Biograph mounted his camera on the front of a trolley traveling over the Brooklyn Bridge. The three 90-foot rolls he created were edited together to complete the journey from Manhattan to Brooklyn, entitled Across the Brooklyn Bridge. As a commission by the Museum of Modern Art for the re-opening of their facility, American avant-garde filmmaker Bill Morrison took this remarkable footage and recombined it with itself to form a new split-screen extrapolation.

over-2015.title: Over
over-2015.desc: Over presents a crime scene. During the course of 9 wide shots, we watch an intriguing story unfold. What's happened in this quiet neighbourhood? A murder, hit-and-run, an accident? The reality is profound, and deeply unexpected.

over-the-fence.title: Over the Fence
over-the-fence.desc: Snitch steals Ginger's (stolen) baseball tickets and takes Ginger's girl to the game. Finding himself without tickets, Ginger dresses as a baseball player and wins the game. A possible debut of the "Glasses" or "Boy" character.

over-the-rainbow-1997.title: Over the Rainbow
over-the-rainbow-1997.desc: An apartment building caretaker with cannibalistic tendencies indulges in his passionate love for Lisa, one of the tenants.

overcomer-2016.title: Overcomer
overcomer-2016.desc: A girl struggles internally with anxiety.

overeating.title: Overeating
overeating.desc: A man greedily eating chicken, whose image is repeated in a loop and appears crumpled. This crumpling accompanies the movement of his jaws.

overstimulated.title: Overstimulated
overstimulated.desc: Two men dressed as children jump up and down, ad nauseum

overtime-2005.title: Overtime
overtime-2005.desc: Little ragdolls find their maker dead in his studio. Unable to understand what truly happened they try to get on with their daily life beside him.
overtime-2005.director: Oury Atlan, Thibaut Berland, Damien Ferrié

overtime-2016.title: Overtime
overtime-2016.desc: It's getting late on a Friday night and Ralph is keen to get out of the office, but the boss won't let him. No big deal, right? It's just that the full moon is rising and Ralph is a werewolf.

overture-1965.title: Ouverture
overture-1965.desc: Short film about the creation of one single life.

overture-to-the-merry-wives-of-windsor.title: Overture to The Merry Wives of Windsor
overture-to-the-merry-wives-of-windsor.desc: Overture to The Merry Wives of Windsor [also known as The Merry Wives of Windsor Overture] is a 1953 American short musical film produced by Johnny Green. The film consists of the MGM Symphony Orchestra playing the Overture to Otto Nicolai's opera The Merry Wives of Windsor, also conducted by Johnny Green. It won an Oscar in 1954 for Best Short Subject, One-Reel.

overture-tannhauser.title: Overture: Tannhäuser
overture-tannhauser.desc: Henry Hadley (1871-1937) conducts the New York Philharmonic Orchestra in the overture to Wagner's "Tannhäuser." Two cameras provide some visual variation: a stationary one that shows Hadley and the full orchestra of more than 80 musicians, and one that does a modest amount of panning and is closer to the musicians, usually showing us about 15 within the frame. All are men, in tuxedos. No words are spoken in this early talkie.

owl-2019.title: Owl
owl-2019.desc: His trainer stands below the tree holding a dead mouse by its tail and a clicker. Dimitri is meant to fly to his trainer. He has missed his cue. A perfectly still film crew is waiting for the owl to make his move. The crew has been shooting in these woods all week and has spotted a baby eagle and it’s mother. Dimitri seems to sense the eagle’s presence. The trainer calls the owl with a whistle and clicks his clicker. Dimitri is not listening.

owl-gets-in-your-eyes.title: Owl Gets in Your Eyes
owl-gets-in-your-eyes.desc: Part of Chris Marker’s Three Video Haikus series, Owl Gets in Your Eyes observes owls and their young in quiet close-up, capturing their shifting expressions and watchful gaze.

an-owl-is-an-owl-is-an-owl.title: An Owl Is an Owl Is an Owl
an-owl-is-an-owl-is-an-owl.desc: Part of Chris Marker’s Bestiaire (Petit Bestiaire) collection, An Owl Is an Owl Is an Owl is a short video meditation on the gaze and movement of owls—sometimes still, sometimes in flight—observed with the quiet, rhythmic attention typical of Marker’s later video work.

the-owl-who-married-a-goose-an-eskimo-le.title: The Owl Who Married a Goose: An Eskimo Legend
the-owl-who-married-a-goose-an-eskimo-le.desc: In this short animation based on an Inuit legend, a goose captures the fancy of an owl, a weakness for which he will pay dearly. The sound effects and voices are Inuktitut, but the animation leaves no doubt as to the unfolding action. A story with the wry humor characteristic of many Inuit tales.

ox.title: Ox
ox.desc: Captured in location with Ambient Sound. Aditional music Sebastian Escofet.

the-oz-witch-project.title: The Oz Witch Project
the-oz-witch-project.desc: Dorothy, the tinman, the cowardly lion and the scarecrow go into the woods near Emerald City to shoot a documentary about the Yellow Brick Road. Unfortunately, they get lost and are never heard from again.

ozzie-of-the-mounted.title: Ozzie of the Mounted
ozzie-of-the-mounted.desc: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, goes in pursuit of Peg-Leg Pete.

ou-en-etes-vous-jean-marie-straub.title: Où en êtes-vous, Jean-Marie Straub ?
ou-en-etes-vous-jean-marie-straub.desc: An initiative from Pompidou Center, filmed by Jean Marie Straub.

the-p-38-pilot.title: The P-38 Pilot
the-p-38-pilot.desc: “For the dispossessed, the excluded, the condemned, fallen from life and loving.” These words are typed across the screen at the outset of THE P-38 PILOT, Bruce Baillie’s experimental video portrait of a former pilot outraged by old age and bitter with regrets. We hear the man's disputatious monologue on the soundtrack: “I’m not the kind of guy to end up in a slime pit… I can’t understand it, see?” Baillie, an established master of 16mm cinematography, uses the video medium to search the man's confined space for rustling movements and leaking colors. Chet Baker sings “There Will Never Be Another You” as the filmmaker bids the pilot a peaceful adieu.

pacer.title: Pacer
pacer.desc: A hyperlapse of Montreal, shot in single frames on a Bolex, capturing a unique journey through time and space across the city.

pacific-231.title: Pacific 231
pacific-231.desc: An engine moves from the roundhouse to a track where it couples with several passenger cars. At 2:10 in the afternoon, it starts a trip out of the station through the countryside to its destination. The film consists of a montage of shots, some close up, of the engine and its gears and wheels. With the accompanying ambient sounds and an orchestral score, the emphasis is on the engine's power and speed. Parallel lines of multiple tracks, telephone wires, and trees confirm a careful composition.

the-pacific-ocean.title: The Pacific Ocean
the-pacific-ocean.desc: Shot on 8mm on the 12-day boat journey between Yokohama and San Francisco, Iimura's The Pacific Ocean consumes the anticipation and uncertainties of a voyage on waves with an obsessive attention on the ripples. (Julian Ross)

the-pact-2011.title: The Pact
the-pact-2011.desc: A young woman finds herself alone in the house of her late mother where an unsettling and sinister presence emerges. Short, remade full length in 2012.

page-miss-glory-1936.title: Page Miss Glory
page-miss-glory-1936.desc: While the rural town of Hicksville anticipates the arrival of one Miss Glory, the bellhop at her modest hotel falls asleep and dreams of paging her at a luxurious metropolitan high rise hotel.

paid-programming-icelandic-ultra-blue.title: Paid Programming: Icelandic Ultra Blue
paid-programming-icelandic-ultra-blue.desc: Learn about a revolutionary new drug (not to mention Nazi gold and chest rashes) in this informative (and fake) infomercial.

paintbrush.title: Paintbrush
paintbrush.desc: Made up entirely of stills, 'Paintbrush' presents portraits of ten users of a fictitious online social networking website. By detailing the information given by each user on their profile, the film explores themes surrounding identity, while also serving as a satire of online social networking.

painted-eightsome.title: Painted Eightsome
painted-eightsome.desc: Margaret Tait described this title as 'An eightsome reel played by Orkney Strathspey and Reel Society, recorded in about 1955 - 1956, later transferred to 35mm optical stock with clear picture and gradually painted over the years. Eights of different things - figures, antlers, or sometimes just blobs in tartan colours - dance their way through the figure of the reel.

the-painted-lady.title: The Painted Lady
the-painted-lady.desc: A lonely young woman lives with her strict father who forbids her to wear make-up. One day at an ice cream social, she meets a young man you seems interested in her. However, unknown to her, he is a burglar who is only interested in breaking into her father's house. One night she is awakened by a noise.

painter-and-ball-4-14.title: Painter and Ball 4-14
painter-and-ball-4-14.desc: Painter and Ball 4-14 is a composite of several simultaneous intentions. The first is a record of the passage of days and seasons: the second is a similar recording made by another artist some thirty years previously: the third, an animation of a headless and limbless homunculus.

painting-covers-art-uncovers.title: Painting covers, art uncovers
painting-covers-art-uncovers.desc: In this experimental video project, originally broadcast on the ZDF television art program "Aspekte," artist Richard Kriesche appears on a TV monitor and delivers an artist statement about the invisible wall between artist and spectator in the televisual medium. Kriesche then paints over a glass canvas, the very invisible wall, between himself and the camera, just as he reappears in front of the TV monitor and delivers the same artist statement. After this, Kriesche paints over the glass of the TV monitor with blue paint, acting as a chrome key effect that slowly uncovers the original image of Kriesche on the monitor, now seeming to drip as the blue paint spills over and Kriesche delivers…

painting-with-joan.title: Painting with Joan
painting-with-joan.desc: Are you curious about Minnesota's #3 public-access painting show? Painting with Joan is coming to the Sundance Film Festival! Watch Joan paint beautiful snowy mountains and debate extraterrestrial sexuality with herself!

the-painting-1972.title: The Painting
the-painting-1972.desc: The Painting intercuts shots of traffic navigating the old-world remnants of downtown Bern, Switzerland, with details from a 15th-century altarpiece, “The Martyrdom of St. Hippolytus”. The painting shows the calm, near-naked saint in a peaceful landscape, a frozen moment before four horses tear his body to pieces while an audience of soigné nobles look on; in the movie’s revised version, Beavers gives it a comparably rarefied psychodramatic jolt, juxtaposing shots of Gregory Markopoulos, bisected by shafts of light, with a torn photo of himself and the recurring image of a shattered windowpane.

a-pair-of-ais-conversing-inside-the-mind.title: A Pair of AIs Conversing Inside the Mind of a Dog
a-pair-of-ais-conversing-inside-the-mind.desc: Two AIs have a conversation inside the mind of a dog as it lays on a pullout mattress joyfully playing with its chew toy. Also a segment of Hayes' experimental feature, "A Subconscious Stream."

pale-blue-eyes.title: Pale Blue Eyes
pale-blue-eyes.desc: This is an ultra rare and unreleased 6 1/2 minute Aryan Kaganof short that was shot in Amsterdam in 1992 but not edited together until 2002 after the director moved back to South Africa. Kaganof merely projected the old 1992 16mm footage onto a screen and recorded it with a digital camera in 2002. For some reason, he opted to not use a tripod, so the camera constantly moves around throughout the short.

palindrome-1964.title: Palindrome
palindrome-1964.desc: A palindrome created on film. Features interaction between a couple with the recurring line 'Madam I'm Adam'.

palindrome-2001.title: Palindrome
palindrome-2001.desc: A word or phrase whose meaning does not change whether spelt backwards or forwards. A young man loses everything he has in one day. He is fired from his job, kicked out of his hotel, betrayed by his colleagues and turned down by an old flame. We see this ordinary tale told backwards in time

palisades-in-palisades.title: Palisades in Palisades
palisades-in-palisades.desc: For this video, Palisades in Palisades, 2014, Rose wanted to expand both her conceptual concerns and her cinematographic repertoire. “I was learning how to make a shot in relation to the content,” she explains, “and how the shots were metaphors for pure sensual material.” The artist accomplished this by using a remote-control camera that could zoom from 200 feet away all the way up to the pores in an individual’s skin. She chose to shoot in New Jersey’s Palisades Interstate Park, a onetime Revolutionary War battleground turned landscaped circuit park that sits atop an ancient cliff.

palm-springs.title: Palm Springs
palm-springs.desc: This short is about a purple dinosaur named Sigmund, who likes to bounce on top of trees. Preserved by the Academy Film Archive in 2011.

palmerston-blvd.title: Palmerston Blvd.
palmerston-blvd.desc: Intimate and elegant, Dan Browne's Palmerston Blvd. depicts the world within and outside a bay window, captured over the course of a year, where seasons sweep by with the speed of a day or a setting sun.

palmipedarium.title: Palmipedarium
palmipedarium.desc: Simon knows ducks quite well. They make noise, fly, swim, some even roll. Sometimes, it's a bit confusing and Simon gets lost.

palms-2015.title: Palms
palms-2015.desc: Musical and mysterious, Mary Helena Clark’s Palms is a modular, sphinx-like film in four parts, comprised of two hands animating stillness, the repeated approach of headlights, a back-and-forth tennis match, and thoughts that emerge like objects.

palo-santo.title: Palo Santo
palo-santo.desc: Palo Santo, a city on a distant planet, on which human beings are a rare commodity, worshipped and idolized by an android society. Olly, along with the final humans, is recruited to perform in a series of bizarre erotic cabarets, for an artificial master known only as The Showman.

pan-0.title: Pan 0
pan-0.desc: Clouds roll by in a static haze.

pan-1.title: Pan 1
pan-1.desc: A pendulum swings by until it comes to a complete stop.

pan-2.title: Pan 2
pan-2.desc: Rain falls and reflects the light.

pan-3.title: Pan 3
pan-3.desc: A journey through a field of corn.

pan-4.title: Pan 4
pan-4.desc: A series of papers flutter in the wind.

pan-697.title: Pan 697
pan-697.desc: A butchered cow is decapitated in this short film by Hollis Frampton.

pan-698.title: Pan 698
pan-698.desc: The camera pans across a field of flowers at extreme speeds.

pan-699.title: Pan 699
pan-699.desc: A little boy celebrates his frog catch.

pan-700.title: Pan 700
pan-700.desc: A series of ghost-like vehicles drive by.

pan-of-the-landscape.title: Pan of the Landscape
pan-of-the-landscape.desc: Christopher Becks’s Pan of the Landscape uses gorgeous Brakhage-like painting on film to un-Brakhage-like ends: spectacular skies combine with the slow, mechanical movement of a silhouetted form to produce a biting melancholy, as if Becks is mourning the film’s removal from the world it glimpses.

pan-american-exposition-by-night.title: Pan-American Exposition by Night
pan-american-exposition-by-night.desc: A great feature of the Pan-American Exposition, as unanimously conceded by all visitors, was the electric illumination of the Exposition grounds at night. After a great deal of experimenting and patience, we succeeded in securing an excellent picture of the buildings at the Pan-American as they appeared when lighted up at night.
pan-american-exposition-by-night.director: Edwin S. Porter, James Blair Smith

panchos-hideaway.title: Pancho's Hideaway
panchos-hideaway.desc: A hot-tempered bandit, Pancho Vanilla, robs a Mexican bank and rushes to his hideout to count the loot. Speedy Gonzales, Mexico's fastest mouse, follows Pancho there, intending to return the money to the bank. He challenges Pancho to a duel and then speeds past him again and again, bringing every cent of the money back to the bank and causing a flustered and enraged Pancho to shoot himself in the feet.

panda-paws.title: Panda Paws
panda-paws.desc: A short film which serves as a prequel to Kung Fu Panda 3 in which Mei Mei and Bao compete with one another at the Spring Festival.

pandora.title: Pandora
pandora.desc: Experimental filmmaker and color cameraman here collaborate in a surrealistic retelling of the old myth. But this is a dream fantasy with no real parallel to Pandora, replete with striking symbols where everything is larger than life--the silhouetted image of a mother and an infant, the profiled view of two sculptured heads spouting smoke and fire.

the-paneless-window-washer.title: The Paneless Window Washer
the-paneless-window-washer.desc: Bluto dirties all of an office building's windows himself, to drum up business for his window cleaning service. When he gets to Olive's stenographer office, about ten floors up, she says no: Popeye's going to wash her windows. And the battle with Popeye is on.

panels-for-the-walls-of-the-world.title: Panels for the Walls of the World

panic-attack.title: Panic Attack!
panic-attack.desc: Giant robots appear out of the mist and attack the city of Montevideo, Uruguay.

panic-in-the-mailroom.title: Panic in the Mailroom
panic-in-the-mailroom.desc: Two Minions are busy at work in the mailroom. One of them, bored, decides to throw a box of expired PX-41 samples into its designated chute.

a-panicky-picnic.title: A Panicky Picnic
a-panicky-picnic.desc: A man and his wife try to enjoy a picnic, but strange and surreal happenings prevent them from doing so.
a-panicky-picnic.director: Segundo de Chomón, Camille de Morlhon

panni.title: Panni
panni.desc: Panni is a visually arresting work in its formal structure and visual expression of colors. The subject matter of the film is a row of bed sheets flapping on a clothesline, drying in the wind. The colors punch through the screen as orange sheets flutter against a green backdrop of grass and trees.

panoramic-view-of-the-arrival-at-perrach.title: Panoramic View of the Arrival at Perrache Station taken from the Train
panoramic-view-of-the-arrival-at-perrach.desc: Panoramic view of the city and then of the train station.

panoramic-view-of-the-arrival-in-aix-les.title: Panoramic View of the Arrival in Aix-les-Bains taken from the Train (Snowy Conditions)
panoramic-view-of-the-arrival-in-aix-les.desc: Panoramic view of the countryside then of the city.

panorama-of-the-grand-canal-taken-from-a.title: Panorama of the Grand Canal Taken from a Boat
panorama-of-the-grand-canal-taken-from-a.desc: Filmed in 1896 by Alexandre Promio for the Lumière company, this short actuality presents one of the earliest traveling shots in cinema. With the camera mounted on a gondola, the film glides along Venice’s Grand Canal, capturing passing gondolas, bustling waterfront activity, and the city’s iconic architecture from a moving perspective. This simple yet groundbreaking technique introduced audiences to a new way of experiencing motion on screen.

panorama-exterior-westinghouse-works.title: Panorama Exterior Westinghouse Works
panorama-exterior-westinghouse-works.desc: The view from a moving train shows some of the Westinghouse interests and the surrounding areas.

panorama-from-top-of-a-moving-train.title: Panorama from Top of a Moving Train
panorama-from-top-of-a-moving-train.desc: With the cameraman atop a moving train car the viewer is given a one minute glimpse of a French urban area.

panorama-of-calcutta.title: Panorama of Calcutta
panorama-of-calcutta.desc: One of the earliest films to be shot in India apparently shows the Calcutta ghats - or does it?

panorama-of-ealing-from-a-moving-tram.title: Panorama of Ealing from a Moving Tram
panorama-of-ealing-from-a-moving-tram.desc: A camera sits on top of a moving train, providing a panoramic view of Ealing (western London) as the train moves.

panorama-of-eiffel-tower.title: Panorama of Eiffel Tower
panorama-of-eiffel-tower.desc: “Showing the entire height of this wonderful structure from the base of the dome and return, with the great Paris Exposition in the background, looking down Champs de Mars. A most realistic picture.” According to Edison film historian Charles Musser, this film features the first camera tilt among the company's surviving oeuvre.

a-panorama-of-indian-scenes-procession.title: A Panorama of Indian Scenes & Procession

panorama-of-machine-co-aisle.title: Panorama of Machine Co. Aisle
panorama-of-machine-co-aisle.desc: A camera on an overhead crane travels down a large, long aisle where men are shown working on large machinery on either side. Carts carrying equipment are shown traveling on rails down the aisles. There are also men walking in the aisles. From Bitzer's Westinghouse Works series.

panorama-during-the-ascent-of-the-eiffel.title: Panorama during the Ascent of the Eiffel Tower
panorama-during-the-ascent-of-the-eiffel.desc: Panorama during the ascent of the Eiffel Tower.

panorama-taken-from-a-tethered-balloon.title: Panorama Taken from a Tethered Balloon
panorama-taken-from-a-tethered-balloon.desc: Street scene shot from a balloon.

panorama-pris-depuis-une-plate-forme-mob.title: Panorama pris depuis une plate-forme mobile

panorama-view-street-car-motor-room.title: Panorama View, Street Car Motor Room
panorama-view-street-car-motor-room.desc: A camera moving forward on an overhead crane gives a traveling view of men working on machinery. Carts carrying parts and pieces of machinery pass by on rails; cranes lift machinery; and men perform their various duties, including hammering objects. (Library of Congress)

panoramic-view-of-the-morecambe-sea-fron.title: Panoramic View of the Morecambe Sea Front
panoramic-view-of-the-morecambe-sea-fron.desc: One long traveling shot through a sea front lined with tourists, workers, and sundry others.

panoramic-view-aisle-b-westinghouse-work.title: Panoramic View, Aisle B, Westinghouse Works
panoramic-view-aisle-b-westinghouse-work.desc: Panoramic View, Aisle B, Westinghouse Works

panta-rhei.title: Panta Rhei
panta-rhei.desc: In 1952, Haanstra made Panta Rhei , another view of Holland through the eyes of a painter and filmmaker. Its poetic images of water, skies and clouds reflect Haanstra's own moods.

pantry-panic.title: Pantry Panic
pantry-panic.desc: Woody's friends warn him that the groundhog has predicted a blizzard. Unconcerned, Woody decides not to go South with his pals. Soon enough, the blizzard sweeps in and destroys the loony woodpecker's stash of food. Facing starvation, a glimmer of hope arrives in the form of a cat. The cat is also starving and it turns into a match of brawn and wits to see who eats who.

pantry-pirate.title: Pantry Pirate
pantry-pirate.desc: Pluto is tied up in the backyard and has been ordered by the maid to stay outside while she prepares a roast. Of course, once Pluto smells the scent of the roast, he makes a beeline for the kitchen. Unfortuantely, staying undiscovered proves difficult for Pluto once he gets inside particularly after he inhales a bucket of soapy water and starts sneezing. Bubbles fill the kitchen and cups are broken at which point the maid comes downstairs. Luckily, Pluto returns to his doghouse leaving the impression that he never left. The maid just shrugs and says, "I could swear it was that dog."

papageno.title: Papageno
papageno.desc: Film shows the story of Papageno (the one from Mozart's opera "The Magic Flute"), who wants a mate, yet has difficulties getting one.

paper-cock-a-doodles.title: Paper Cock-a-Doodles
paper-cock-a-doodles.desc: Female magicians turn people into origami roosters and vice versa.

paper-trail.title: Paper Trail
paper-trail.desc: Hand-drawn animation with ink, white-out and collage.

paperman.title: Paperman
paperman.desc: An urban office worker finds that paper airplanes are instrumental in meeting a girl in ways he never expected.

papers-please-2018.title: Papers, Please
papers-please-2018.desc: An official adaptation of the award winning game "Papers, Please" by Lucas Pope.

papillons.title: Papillons
papillons.desc: Mathematical functions are the basis for a science film on contour plots and an art film. Both are shown simultaneously at a two screen production for an IEEE conference in NYC. Beauty in Science & Art.

papiroflexia.title: Papiroflexia
papiroflexia.desc: Papiroflexia (Spanish for “Origami”) is the animated tale of Fred, a chubby man with a passion for paper folding, who wants to change the world with his art.

papa-wrestling.title: Papá Wrestling
papa-wrestling.desc: After bullies steal his son's lunch-box, a retired wrestler goes on a violent rampage to avenge him and bring justice to the school.

parabola.title: Parabola
parabola.desc: Parabola is a celebration of film’s ability to create new ways of seeing the forms around us. Creating juxtapositions between light/shadow, stasis/motion, and form/music, this black-and-white short invites us to see the parabolic curve, or “nature’s poetry,” as both invigorating and beguiling.

parade-1962.title: Parade
parade-1962.desc: Filmed in Belgrade in 1962, Parade documents the city’s engagement with the annual May Day celebration by largely ignoring the formal procession. Instead, Dušan Makavejev records the informal moments surrounding it: workers, officials, wanderers, and organizers negotiating space, hierarchy, and appearance. Shot with a detached, humorous eye, the film assembles a mosaic of everyday behavior that reveals the contrast between official ceremony and lived social reality.

parade-of-the-award-nominees.title: Parade of the Award Nominees
parade-of-the-award-nominees.desc: Mickey Mouse grand marshals a parade of 1932 Academy Award nominees. Minnie Mouse leads the marching band and Clarabelle Cow rolls out a carpet for the celebrities. Wallace Beery marches in boxing gloves with Jackie Cooper as his footman. Lynn Fontanne and Alfred Lunt walk the route together. Helen Hayes shuffles down the carpet. Fredric March appears as both Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. Marie Dressler follows, trailing a corset and an alarm clock. Pluto brings up the rear of the parade.

parade-of-the-wooden-soldiers.title: Parade of the Wooden Soldiers
parade-of-the-wooden-soldiers.desc: A toy version of Betty Boop drops in on a small toy shop. The other toys come to life and crown her their queen. Then the cartoon quickly turns into Fleischer's idea of King Kong.

the-parade-1987.title: The Parade
the-parade-1987.desc: The harvest season recalls past time, gives rise to reflections, memories. The logic of the aftermath of events is replaced here by the logic of memory.

paradigm.title: Paradigm
paradigm.desc: William Hoyland stars as a nameless protagonist who speaks to the camera in a fabricated language and, though the course of the film, transforms from young and verbose, to old and inarticulate.

paradise-1984.title: Paradise
paradise-1984.desc: A magnificent bird performs for the Emperor inside a glittering palace. Its plumage is a blaze of colour. A blackbird, watching enviously, strives to acquire what he so desperately covets, only to discover that a golden cage can't compete with the open skies.

paradise-lost-2015-1.title: Paradise Lost?
paradise-lost-2015-1.desc: After discovering that John Milton is buried within London's Barbican grounds, Iain Forsyth & Jane Pollard reimagined his epic poem ‘Paradise Lost’ as part of Doug Aitken's Station to Station project. The piece uses the architecture and atmosphere of the Barbican to update the story, which is told in three parts.

the-paradise-next-door.title: The Paradise Next Door
the-paradise-next-door.desc: As America's largest retirement community continues to expand, cracks, both literal and metaphysical, are suddenly opening beneath the senior utopia.

parallax-2008.title: Parallax
parallax-2008.desc: Christopher Becks’ video, Parallax, is converted from richly colored 16mm footage. He addresses the practice of landscape/travel films by presenting scenes that seem to connote wandering, and searching for something.

paranoia-2010.title: Paranoia
paranoia-2010.desc: Short film using the paranoia of Richard Nixon to explore how a similar outlook on life has been propagated on a larger social scale in the new media age and the resulting moral panics and immobilisation of politics. Screen during the fourth episode of the second series of Charlie Brooker's Newswipe.

paraiso-2013.title: Paraíso
paraiso-2013.desc: 'Paraíso' follows three Mexican immigrants who risk their lives as window washers, spending each and every day rappelling down the tallest skyscrapers in Chicago. Along the way, they share their thoughts on working, mortality, and the people they observe inside the high-rises they clean.

parcelle.title: Parcelle
parcelle.desc: Composed frame by frame in the camera, Parcelle (fragment, particle or bit) rests upon the alternate appearance and variable duration of tiny colored squares or circles placed on black backgrounds and inserted in series between plain white or colored images, creating optical superimpositions on the screen.

parental-leave.title: Parental Leave
parental-leave.desc: "Images and sounds culled from the first few months with my daughter, sometimes resembling that of a family group chat, where pictures and videos are shared; small moments. The film is full of joy, and full of uncertainty, barely holding itself together." A companion piece to 'My Heart is Walking Around Outside of my Body'.

the-parents-room.title: The Parents' Room
the-parents-room.desc: A family gathers around a bed to sing a lament to their own deaths, accompanied by a blackbird.

parfum-fraise.title: Parfum Fraise
parfum-fraise.desc: Makoto is doing his best to raise his 7-year-old son Kazuki. Despite his best intentions, the violence that was once his life comes back to bite him, and he will have no choice but to face it, before the eyes of his son, who he always tried to protect.
parfum-fraise.director: Samuel Klughertz, Alix Arrault, Jules Rigolle, Martin Hurmane

paris-at-dawn.title: Paris at Dawn
paris-at-dawn.desc: Johan van der Keuken's first film is a uniquely beautiful portrait of Paris at dawn.
paris-at-dawn.director: Johan van der Keuken, James Blue

paris-on-parade.title: Paris on Parade
paris-on-parade.desc: This Traveltalks short showcases the Paris International Exposition of 1937. It features a tour of the pavillions of several nations, as well as the spectacular water and light displays.

paris-capital-of-the-19th-century.title: Paris, Capital of the 19th Century
paris-capital-of-the-19th-century.desc: An essay/experimental film about Walter Benjamin's Passagen-Werk by Benjamin Bardou.

paris-le-7-janvier-1988.title: Paris, le 7 Janvier 1988
paris-le-7-janvier-1988.desc: Film made for the filmaker's almanach, a project of Owen O'Toole. Film based on the progress/unrolling of a (typical) day in my life from the early hour of the morning. Full of the daily errands to the evening on my way to work in the suburbs of Paris.

park-film.title: Park Film
park-film.desc: This is not so much a film about a park, or a record of the people passing through the park. Here the camera is not a passive observer, nor is it used as a surveillance device. Rather, the camera in Park Film, like the passers by who trigger its shutter, is an active participant in the interaction between a park and the city which surrounds it.

the-park-2015.title: The Park
the-park-2015.desc: Portrait of youths in an abandoned amusement park in Casablanca, in meaningful tableaus inspired by social media. "I am here, I exist."

parkgate-iron-and-steel-co-rotherham.title: Parkgate Iron and Steel Co., Rotherham
parkgate-iron-and-steel-co-rotherham.desc: Edwardian workers react to the camera at one of Rotherham's major employers.

parking-2002.title: Parking
parking-2002.desc: A parking lot attendant loses his temper when his working place is invaded by a blade of grass. A furious battle ensues.

parlez-vous-woo.title: Parlez Vous Woo
parlez-vous-woo.desc: Olive is so captived by "The International", a radio personality with a French accent, that she'd rather stay home than go out on a date with Popeye. Bluto, overhearing this, comes to the door as the character.

the-parlor.title: The Parlor
the-parlor.desc: A group of people are gathered in a room, which is a "live" depiction of a typical Internet chat room. Some pretends to be much younger than they are, to chat up minors. Two of them falls victim of their own scam in a surprising way.

part-time-pal.title: Part Time Pal
part-time-pal.desc: Tom is given the task of guarding the fridge during the night by Mammy-Two-Shoes, but as soon as he has started he is tricked by Jerry into falling into the basement, where he lands in a barrel of cider. Now drunk, Tom staggers around in the house getting up to no good with Jerry.

a-partial-history-of-the-natural-world-1.title: A Partial History of the Natural World, 1965
a-partial-history-of-the-natural-world-1.desc: A meditative exploration of the violent struggle for independence in southeast Asia and butterfly metamorphosis. Framed by excerpts from Sylvia Plath’s poem “Tulips,” A Partial History of the Natural World, 1965 reminds us that comfort is a privilege and denial of the suffering of others is not an option. Scored by a 1965 performance of Bartok’s “Solo for Violin 3.”

particles-in-space.title: Particles in Space
particles-in-space.desc: Lye completed his last great film a few months before his death at the age of 78. The film returned to the black-and-white techniques of Free Radicals. Lye created what he called “vibrant little images” or “zig-zags” with a sense of “zizz”. The clusters of small scratches gave the film a unique texture – the images looked rough but were in fact extremely subtle. The title Particles in Space referred to flashes of energy of the kind sometimes seen by astronauts in space. The soundtrack combined “Jumping Dance Drums” from the Bahamas with drum music by the Yoruba of Nigeria and the sounds of Lye’s metal kinetic sculptures. The opening titles demonstrated Lye’s mastery of the scratching of…

particularly-now-in-spring.title: Particularly Now, in Spring
particularly-now-in-spring.desc: It's sports day and a seventeen-year-old boy prepares to compete, as he has many times before. Only this time it's different, his childhood is behind him, different feelings, emotions and desires engulf him as he watches his classmates. His life is about to change.

the-card-game-1896.title: The Card Game
the-card-game-1896.desc: Three men are sitting around a table, two of them playing a game of Écarté. When the game is over, a domestic serves drinks.

game-of-boules.title: Game of Boules
game-of-boules.desc: Friends and relatives playing a game of boules, arguing about who's team is winning.

game-of-backgammon.title: Game of Backgammon
game-of-backgammon.desc: Two people are playing backgammon while others watch. The player cheats, his partner protests: the man closes the game box.

partly-cloudy.title: Partly Cloudy
partly-cloudy.desc: Everyone knows that the stork delivers babies, but where do the storks get the babies from?
